html:
SMTO-EXE-0178 — That name is already used in this spreadsheet

GUID: 6197f08b-6bf5-5f0f-9024-26dbccabff75
Slug: office-object-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to add or rename a sheet, table or named range, but that name is already taken in this workbook. Names that differ only in capital letters count as the same. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the workbook and look at the sheet tabs, table names and named ranges to see which name is already taken. Remember that "Sales" and "sales" count as the same name. Excel names must be unique, and SMTO refuses to create a second object with the same name.
  2. Ask SMTO to repeat the step with a different name, for example "Sales 2026" instead of "Sales". A name that isn't in use lets SMTO add or rename the item without confusing it with the existing one.
  3. If you actually meant to change the item that already has that name, tell SMTO to list the workbook's sheets or tables first and then change that existing item. SMTO can change an existing item only when it picks it from a fresh list of what is in the workbook.

What success looks like

  • SMTO creates the new copy of the workbook and the new or renamed sheet, table or named range appears with the name you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name you tried, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An Excel operation was rejected because the requested new sheet, table or named-range name already exists in the workbook under a case-insensitive comparison.

What this means

  • A new sheet or table name conflicts with an existing name under its case-insensitive uniqueness checks. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • A new sheet or table name conflicts with an existing name under its case-insensitive uniqueness checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current sheet/table names and exact occurrence references before choosing a new unique name.

How to fix it

  • Check excel_sheets, excel_tables or excel_named_ranges for the conflicting name: sheet names are unique case-insensitively per workbook, table names across the whole workbook, and named ranges within their workbook or sheet scope. Retry with a unique name, or use the returned ref of the existing object if the intent was to change it.
  • Choose a unique sheet/table name or an exact previewed occurrence reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a unique sheet/table name or an exact previewed occurrence reference.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended new object uses a valid unique name, or an existing exact object is deliberately selected.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
